editor_note: All three rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally. [15] keeps the seven-digit code ("kode verifikasi tujuh digit"), [21] keeps the UI labels "Account ID"/"Details", and in [29] the prefix example (`physics-101-john-doe`, default `open-student`), the no-credit-card caveat and "pengalih akun pada header halaman" all match the English.

Both rewritten entries keep the English meaning: in entry 10, lower approximation degree still means more approximation, more deviation from the input matrix and fewer gates, and the at-most-three-CX caveat is kept. Three wording problems remain. Entry 10 uses "sebuah sirkuit" and "gate diskrit" in the same paragraph as "Circuit" and "Gate", so one term is spelled two ways. It also uses "arbitrari apapun", which is non-standard; natural Indonesian is "sembarang" and "apa pun". Entry 25 renders "pass a list" as "melewatkan daftar", which usually means "skip/miss" in Indonesian. "memberikan" or "meneruskan" is clearer here.

examples.source: you can also pass a list of integers
examples.translation: kamu juga bisa melewatkan daftar bilangan bulat
examples.suggested: kamu juga bisa memberikan daftar bilangan bulat
examples.why: 'melewatkan' usually means 'to skip/miss'. It is a calque of 'pass (an argument)' and can read as 'skip the list'. 'memberikan'/'meneruskan' says it without that ambiguity.

examples.source: a matrix representation of a circuit is converted to discrete gates
examples.translation: representasi matriks sebuah sirkuit dikonversi menjadi gate diskrit
examples.suggested: representasi matriks sebuah Circuit dikonversi menjadi Gate diskrit
examples.why: The same entry (and the rest of the page) uses 'Circuit'/'Gate', so 'sirkuit'/'gate' here is a within-paragraph inconsistency.

examples.source: any arbitrary two-qubit operation
examples.translation: operasi dua-Qubit arbitrari apapun
examples.suggested: sembarang operasi dua-Qubit
examples.why: 'arbitrari' is not standard Indonesian and 'apapun' should be written 'apa pun'. 'sembarang' is the natural technical word.

editor_note: None of the 11 rewritten entries changes the meaning. The caveats in [25] (the visualizations ignore measurements and differ from the QPU) and [76] (phase disks do not alter the circuit) are kept, and so is the "not the same, even for a single qubit" point in [163]. The problems are terminology splits and calques. The heading [126] and entries [22]-[24] and [76] use "cakram fase", but [163] links "[phase disk]" in English. Entry [166] half-translates "quantum phase" as "phase kuantum", while [23] and [16] use the Indonesian "fase". Entry [95] calques "one layer at a time" as "satu lapisan sekaligus" ("sekaligus" means "at once") and "steps through" as "melangkah melalui". Entry [163] has stiff phrasing: "lebih memberi pemahaman" and a sentence-initial "Memang,".

examples.source: It steps through a simulation of your circuit, one layer at a time
examples.translation: Mode ini melangkah melalui simulasi Circuit-mu, satu lapisan sekaligus
examples.suggested: Mode ini menjalankan simulasi Circuit-mu lapis demi lapis
examples.why: 'sekaligus' means 'at once/simultaneously', so 'satu lapisan sekaligus' is a confusing calque. 'melangkah melalui' is literal translationese.

examples.source: The color of each bar represents the quantum phase (${\varphi_k}$).
examples.translation: Warna setiap batang merepresentasikan phase kuantum (${\varphi_k}$).
examples.suggested: Warna setiap batang merepresentasikan fase kuantum (${\varphi_k}$).
examples.why: This mixes English and Indonesian. Elsewhere the file uses 'fase' (entry [23] 'Fase vektor status', entry [16] 'Gate fase').

examples.source: Indeed, like the [phase disk](#phase-disk), the Bloch sphere gives a *local* view
examples.translation: Memang, seperti [phase disk](#phase-disk), Bloch sphere memberikan tampilan *lokal*
examples.suggested: Seperti [cakram fase](#phase-disk), Bloch sphere memberikan tampilan *lokal*
examples.why: The linked section heading [126] and entries [22]-[24] and [76] say 'cakram fase', so the English link text is inconsistent with them. 'Memang,' is a calque of 'Indeed,'.

examples.source: it is more insightful to take a *global* view
examples.translation: lebih memberi pemahaman untuk mengambil sudut pandang *global*
examples.suggested: akan lebih mudah dipahami bila kita mengambil sudut pandang *global*
examples.why: 'lebih memberi pemahaman untuk' is a stiff literal rendering of 'more insightful'.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries match their English: entry 23 renders ideal/noisy simulation as "kondisi ideal … dan kondisi berisik" and "sebagai fungsi kedalaman Circuit", and entry 37 keeps the caveat that PEA "tidak bisa disimulasikan dengan `qiskit_aer`" and renders "work best" as "faktor amplifikasi noise mana yang paling cocok".

None of the 16 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The conditions and caveats are all kept: the dense-circuit warning for DD in [11], the XX default in [14], the 3x folding factor in [43], max_overhead 100 and its effect on precision in [70], and the v0.50.0 noise-learning notes in [60]/[71]. A native editor would still fix four small things. Entry [47] ends in the fragment "Opsi-opsi penting berikut ini:", which has no predicate. Entry [56] drops "corresponding" from "the corresponding learned noise model". Entry [19] uses "menjepit" for "sandwiching", where "mengapit" reads more naturally. Entry [43] uses the bare adjective "uniter" as a noun where "operator uniter" is expected.

examples.source: The following options are notable:
examples.translation: Opsi-opsi penting berikut ini:
examples.suggested: Berikut beberapa opsi yang penting:
examples.why: The Indonesian is a noun phrase with no predicate, so it reads as an unfinished sentence before the list.

examples.source: proportional to the corresponding learned noise model
examples.translation: yang proporsional dengan model noise yang dipelajari
examples.suggested: yang proporsional dengan model noise terpelajari yang bersesuaian (untuk lapisan tersebut)
examples.why: Dropping 'corresponding' loses the point that each layer is amplified by its own learned model. The meaning is mostly still there, so this is minor.

examples.source: sandwiching a chosen set of gates with randomly chosen single-qubit Pauli gates
examples.translation: menjepit sekumpulan Gate yang dipilih dengan Gate Pauli satu qubit
examples.suggested: mengapit sekumpulan Gate yang dipilih dengan Gate Pauli satu qubit
examples.why: 'Menjepit' means to pinch or clamp. 'Mengapit' (to flank on both sides) is the natural image for placing gates before and after.

examples.source: replacing a unitary $U$ with $U U^\dagger U$
examples.translation: menggantikan uniter $U$ dengan $U U^\dagger U$
examples.suggested: mengganti operator uniter $U$ dengan $U U^\dagger U$
examples.why: 'Uniter' is an adjective and sounds odd used alone as a noun. Indonesian technical writing normally says 'operator uniter'. 'Mengganti' is also more natural than 'menggantikan' here.

editor_note: All six rewritten entries are faithful and natural; for example, entry 14 keeps the rule that the later setting wins ("yang dipakai adalah nilai yang ditetapkan setelah inisialisasi"), and entry 16 keeps the copy semantics ("mengubah dictionary atau instance opsi asli tidak memengaruhi opsi yang dimiliki primitif").

All six rewritten entries keep the English meaning, including the shot-count rationale in [26] ("sampel di sektor partikel yang tepat ... aproksimasi awal distribusi bilangan okupansi ground-state") and the hedge in [27] ("sangat bergantung pada sistem dan hardware ... akurasi kimia dapat dicapai"), with the informal "kamu" register throughout.

None of the three rewritten entries (8, 27, 80) changes the meaning: the "only needed if" condition in 80 and the "Complete Step 1, then skip to" route in 27 both survive. A native editor would still change four things. Entry 8 writes "sistem Mirip UNIX" with a capital M mid-sentence (should be "mirip UNIX"). Entry 27 renders "skip to" as "lanjut ke", which loses the sense of skipping Steps 2-5, and it leaves the link text in English ("Build the standalone library") although the target heading is rendered as "Bangun library standalone". Entry 80 uses the non-standard "mengkompilasi" and "menautkan", where the rest of the page uses "mengompilasi" and "di-link".

examples.source: for UNIX-like systems
examples.translation: untuk sistem Mirip UNIX
examples.suggested: untuk sistem mirip UNIX
examples.why: The capital M only makes sense in the heading or link label. In running text the adjective should be lowercase.

examples.source: Complete Step 1, then skip to [Build the standalone library]
examples.translation: Selesaikan Langkah 1, lalu lanjut ke [Build the standalone library]
examples.suggested: Selesaikan Langkah 1, lalu langsung lompat ke [Bangun library standalone]
examples.why: 'lanjut ke' reads as 'continue on to' and loses the instruction to skip Steps 2-5. The English link text also does not match the translated heading the reader will see on the page.

examples.source: compile and link pure C programs
examples.translation: mengkompilasi dan menautkan program C murni
examples.suggested: mengompilasi dan me-link program C murni
examples.why: Entries 16 and 85 use the standard form 'mengompilasi', and entries 27 and 65 use 'di-link'. This entry uses 'mengkompilasi' and 'menautkan', so the same terms appear in two forms within one file.

editor_note: Entry 22 keeps the English meaning. The dependence on both the problem instance and later processing, the hedged "mungkin mencapai kualitas solusi akhir yang serupa" and the closing call to judge the whole workflow are all intact. It has two terminology slips against the rest of the page. It leaves "post-processing" in English, but entries 10 and 16 use "pasca-pemrosesan". examples.source: after equivalent post-processing
examples.translation: setelah post-processing yang setara
examples.suggested: setelah pasca-pemrosesan yang setara
examples.why: Entries 10 and 16 render post-processing as 'pasca-pemrosesan'. Leaving it in English here breaks consistency within the page.

examples.source: the complete optimization workflow
examples.translation: keseluruhan alur kerja optimisasi
examples.suggested: keseluruhan alur kerja optimasi
examples.why: Everywhere else the page uses 'optimasi' (entries 0, 6, 7, 36, 68). 'optimisasi' is the only exception.

editor_note: Of the six rewritten entries, none would mislead a learner. Entries 8, 24, 25 and 41 are accurate and read naturally: "bisa di-broadcast" / "tidak bisa di-broadcast", "deviasi standar" and "informasi spesifik implementasi" all keep the English meaning. The problem is in entries 64 and 65. They keep the English word order and put "API" after the link ("Tinjau [`qiskit-ibm-runtime` Estimator] API."). Indonesian puts the head noun first, and the entries just before them (61, 62) already do this correctly ("Tinjau API [primitif Qiskit SDK]"), so the four items in the same Recommendations list no longer match each other.

examples.source: Review the [`qiskit-ibm-runtime` Estimator](...) API.
examples.translation: Tinjau [`qiskit-ibm-runtime` Estimator](...) API.
examples.suggested: Tinjau API [Estimator `qiskit-ibm-runtime`](...).
examples.why: This keeps the English modifier-before-noun order. Indonesian puts the head noun first, and the sibling entries 61 and 62 already write "Tinjau API [...]", so this item doesn't match the rest of the list.

examples.source: -  Review the [`qiskit-ibm-runtime` Sampler](...) API.
examples.translation: -  Tinjau [`qiskit-ibm-runtime` Sampler](...) API.
examples.suggested: -  Tinjau API [Sampler `qiskit-ibm-runtime`](...).
examples.why: Same English-order problem as entry 64, and it doesn't match the pattern entries 61 and 62 set in the same Recommendations admonition.

editor_note: The four rewritten entries (14, 17, 24, 26) keep the English meaning, including the entry-26 caveats ("bukan merupakan batasan keras", "Performa di perangkat lain bisa berbeda", "10.000 shot per Circuit"), and they read naturally, e.g. "out of the box" becomes "tanpa perlu konfigurasi tambahan" and "swap in" becomes "beralih ke Sampler dan Estimator Q-CTRL".

None of the three rewritten entries changes the meaning. Entry 7 keeps the negation right ("tidak bisa saling melihat, meskipun mereka bisa mengakses sumber daya yang sama"). Entry 21 keeps "kumpulan izin minimum" and the "Pertama… Selanjutnya" order. There are two small slips. The heading in entry 20 uses the English "instance", while entry 21 and the rest of the page use "instans". examples.source: 4. Create access groups for instances
examples.translation: 4. Buat grup akses untuk instance
examples.suggested: 4. Buat grup akses untuk instans
examples.why: The rest of the page, including entry 21 directly below it, says "instans". The English "instance" in this heading is inconsistent with that.

examples.source: users in your account cannot see each other ... Choose the appropriate value for your environment.
examples.translation: pengguna di akunmu tidak bisa saling melihat ... Pilih nilai yang sesuai untuk lingkunganmu.
examples.suggested: pengguna di akun Anda tidak bisa saling melihat ... Pilih nilai yang sesuai untuk lingkungan Anda.
examples.why: Neighboring entries (8, 11, 12, 15) address the reader as "Anda". The -mu forms in this rewritten entry switch the page's form of address partway through.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are faithful and natural: [18] "untuk detail lengkap tentang kelas tersebut" and [25] "tidak perlu diinstansiasi kalau kamu menyetel opsi setelah menginisialisasi primitif" keep the condition and negation intact, and they use the page's own terms ("primitif", "kamu").

The rewritten heading in entry 5 renders "Dynamical decoupling" as "Dekopling dinamis". That doesn't match the body right below it, where entries 6 and 7 keep the English term ("menerapkan dynamical decoupling", "urutan dynamical decoupling XX"). Indonesian quantum-computing writing normally keeps this technique name in English. "Dekopling" is an unusual loan-coinage that learners won't find in the literature. The meaning is still recognizable, so this doesn't mislead, but the heading should use the same term as the body.

examples.source: Dynamical decoupling {#dynamical-decoupling}
examples.translation: Dekopling dinamis {#dynamical-decoupling}
examples.suggested: Dynamical decoupling {#dynamical-decoupling}
examples.why: The heading's term doesn't match entries 6-7, which keep 'dynamical decoupling' in English. That's also the usual form in Indonesian quantum-computing texts. 'Dekopling dinamis' is a non-standard coinage, recognizable but inconsistent within the file.

editor_note: Rewritten entry 6 is faithful and natural: "tidak cukup hanya dengan menyadari" keeps the "more to understanding than" point, "mengukur sebagian tapi tidak semua" keeps the partial-measurement setup, and *korelasi* / *entanglement* match the English emphasis.

Both rewritten entries keep the English meaning and would not mislead a learner. Entry 5 is fine: "membangun kapabilitas yang diperlukan secara efektif, agar bisa memulai inisiatif kuantum dengan sukses". Entry 8 has two small problems a native editor would fix. "akan terutama bermanfaat" is a stiff calque of "will be of particular use". "project leaders" became "manajer proyek", which is a slightly different role from a leader, though a defensible one.

examples.source: It will be of particular use to organizations new to quantum computing.
examples.translation: Kursus ini akan terutama bermanfaat bagi organisasi yang baru mengenal komputasi kuantum.
examples.suggested: Kursus ini sangat bermanfaat terutama bagi organisasi yang baru mengenal komputasi kuantum.
examples.why: 'akan terutama bermanfaat' copies the English future tense plus adverb word for word and reads stiffly. Indonesian would normally drop 'akan' and put 'terutama' before the beneficiary.

examples.source: project leaders in large enterprises
examples.translation: manajer proyek di perusahaan besar
examples.suggested: pemimpin proyek di perusahaan besar
examples.why: 'Leaders' became 'managers', a slightly narrower role. This is minor and does not mislead, but 'pemimpin proyek' stays closer to the source and matches 'pemimpin' earlier in the same sentence.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries keep the meaning and the informal "kamu/-mu" register. Nothing that would mislead a learner was found: the Credly data list, the global sharing clause and the privacy links are all intact. Entry 5 uses "meningkatkan" twice ("meningkatkan kursus ini" and "meningkatkan penawaran konten"), and "penawaran konten" is a stiff calque of "content offering". In entry 11 both link texts, "[di sini.]", now hold the sentence's full stop inside the link, which differs from the English "[here](…)." markup.

examples.source: Your feedback will be used to enhance our content offering and user experience.
examples.translation: Masukanmu akan digunakan untuk meningkatkan penawaran konten dan pengalaman pengguna kami.
examples.suggested: Masukanmu akan kami gunakan untuk menyempurnakan konten dan pengalaman pengguna kami.
examples.why: 'penawaran konten' is a literal calque, and a second 'meningkatkan' repeats the verb from the sentence before; 'menyempurnakan konten' reads more natively.

examples.source: The IBM Privacy Statement can be viewed [here](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/).
examples.translation: Pernyataan Privasi IBM dapat dilihat [di sini.](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/)
examples.suggested: Pernyataan Privasi IBM dapat dilihat [di sini](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/).
examples.why: The full stop has moved inside the link text in both links. The English keeps it outside, so put it back after the link.

editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries (2, 4, 5, 7) would mislead a learner. The threshold-theorem conditions ("selama tingkat noise berada di bawah nilai ambang tertentu", "*tidak* bergantung pada ukuran Circuit") and the decode/re-encode risk argument keep their meaning. Two phrasings would still get an editor's pen. In entry 4, "tidak pernah melepas perlindungan" makes the logical qubits sound like they actively let go of the protection; "tidak pernah lepas dari perlindungan" is the natural form. In entry 7, "tetapi yang krusial *tidak* bergantung" is ambiguous, because it can read as "the crucial one does not depend". Saying "tetapi, yang krusial, nilai ini *tidak* bergantung" fixes that.

examples.source: logical qubits that never go without the protection of a quantum error correcting code
examples.translation: qubit *logis* yang tidak pernah melepas perlindungan kode koreksi kesalahan kuantum
examples.suggested: qubit *logis* yang tidak pernah lepas dari perlindungan kode koreksi kesalahan kuantum
examples.why: 'melepas' is transitive and implies the qubit actively removes the protection; 'lepas dari' is the idiomatic way to say 'never without'.

examples.source: but critically it does *not* depend on the size of the quantum circuit being implemented
examples.translation: tetapi yang krusial *tidak* bergantung pada ukuran Circuit kuantum yang diimplementasikan
examples.suggested: tetapi, yang krusial, nilai ini *tidak* bergantung pada ukuran sirkuit kuantum yang diimplementasikan
examples.why: Without a subject or commas, 'yang krusial' reads as the subject ('the crucial one'), which blurs the emphasis that the threshold itself is independent of circuit size.

editor_note: Neither rewritten entry would mislead a learner. Entry 2 keeps both hedges: "tampaknya cocok" for "seem likely to be well-suited", and "Tidak semua ... tapi banyak" for the claim that not every code is a stabilizer code. The problems are in entry 3 and are only about how it reads. "kembali meninjau kode repetisi untuk kedua kalinya" says "again" twice, and the list "tugas fundamental encoding, mendeteksi kesalahan, serta mengoreksi" puts the bare English noun "encoding" next to Indonesian verbs, so the list reads unevenly. "properti dasar" would also read more naturally as "sifat dasar" in a math context.

examples.source: We'll then go back and take a second look at the repetition code
examples.translation: Kita kemudian akan kembali meninjau kode repetisi untuk kedua kalinya
examples.suggested: Kita kemudian akan meninjau ulang kode repetisi
examples.why: 'kembali' and 'untuk kedua kalinya' both mean 'again', which is redundant and reads like a word-for-word calque of 'go back and take a second look'.

examples.source: basic properties of stabilizer codes, and how the fundamental tasks of encoding, detecting errors, and correcting those errors can be performed
examples.translation: properti dasar kode stabilizer, dan bagaimana tugas fundamental encoding, mendeteksi kesalahan, serta mengoreksi kesalahan tersebut bisa dilakukan
examples.suggested: sifat-sifat dasar kode stabilizer, serta bagaimana tugas-tugas mendasar, yaitu encoding, deteksi kesalahan, dan koreksi kesalahan, bisa dilakukan
examples.why: The list puts the English noun 'encoding' next to Indonesian verbs ('mendeteksi', 'mengoreksi'), so the items are not parallel. 'Tugas fundamental encoding' is a stiff calque, and 'sifat' is the usual Indonesian math word for 'properties'.

editor_note: None of the six rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The no-solution caveat (entry 7), the deterministic-versus-probabilistic O(N) argument (entry 12) and the Or-versus-Search distinction (entry 23) all match the English. The remaining problems are small wording choices. Entry 7 uses "di mana" for "for which", a calqued relative clause where "yang memenuhi" is the usual form. Entry 19 renders "precise statement" as "pernyataan ... yang tepat", which reads more like "the correct/appropriate statement" than "the precise statement". Entry 9's "tidak punya harapan untuk memahami" and "selain memiliki kemampuan untuk" follow the English wording too literally.

examples.line_approx: Yang dilakukan algoritma Grover adalah mencari string $x\in\Sigma^n$ di mana $f(x) = 1$.
examples.source: search for a string $x\in\Sigma^n$ for which $f(x) = 1$
examples.translation: mencari string $x\in\Sigma^n$ di mana $f(x) = 1$
examples.suggested: mencari string $x\in\Sigma^n$ yang memenuhi $f(x) = 1$
examples.why: "di mana" used as a relative pronoun is a well-known English calque in Indonesian technical writing, and "yang memenuhi" is the natural mathematical phrasing.

examples.line_approx: Berikut adalah pernyataan masalah yang tepat
examples.source: Here's a precise statement of the problem
examples.translation: Berikut adalah pernyataan masalah yang tepat
examples.suggested: Berikut adalah pernyataan masalah secara presisi (formal)
examples.why: "yang tepat" reads as "the correct/appropriate statement" rather than "a precise statement". The meaning is recoverable from context, but the nuance of formal precision is weakened.

examples.line_approx: kita tidak punya harapan untuk memahami Circuit tersebut ... (selain memiliki kemampuan untuk mengevaluasinya ...)
examples.source: we have no hope of making sense of the circuit by examining it (beyond having the ability to evaluate it on selected input strings)
examples.translation: kita tidak punya harapan untuk memahami Circuit tersebut dengan memeriksanya (selain memiliki kemampuan untuk mengevaluasinya pada string input yang dipilih)
examples.suggested: mustahil bagi kita memahami rangkaian itu hanya dengan memeriksanya (selain bahwa kita bisa mengevaluasinya pada string input yang dipilih)
examples.why: "tidak punya harapan untuk" and "selain memiliki kemampuan untuk" copy the English structure word for word. The meaning is intact, but a native writer would phrase it more directly.

editor_note: None of the four rewritten headings would mislead a learner. The partial-trace headings [57], [74] and [84] use "partial trace", which matches the body text ([29], [63], [85]). The one problem is heading [13], "State produk", which translates the term, while the body right under it defines it in English as "*product states*" ([15]) and keeps using "product states" in [17] and [27]. The reader meets two names for one concept, so the heading and the body should use the same one.

examples.source: Product states {#product-states}
examples.translation: State produk {#product-states}
examples.suggested: State produk (product states) {#product-states}, or render the body's *product states* in [15]/[17]/[27] as *state produk* so the heading and the definition match
examples.why: The heading's translated term doesn't match the English *product states* that the body uses and defines right under it. The meaning is right, but the reader gets two names for the same concept.

editor_note: Rewritten entry 9 is faithful and natural: "badging exam" is rendered as "ujian lencana", consistent with the heading "Mendapatkan lencana" in entry 8; the optional "if you wish" is kept as "jika kamu mau"; and the file's "kamu" register holds throughout.

All four rewritten entries (4, 6, 11, 16) keep the meaning, and none of them would mislead a learner. The Credly privacy notice in entry 16 is faithful and uses the kamu register consistently. Entry 4 renders "substantial discussion" as "diskusi substantif", which is a false-friend calque: "substantif" means essential or substantive, not extensive. "pembahasan yang cukup mendalam" is better. Entry 6 renders "some experience" as "sedikit pengalaman", which slightly understates the prerequisite. "sudah memiliki pengalaman" fits better.

examples.source: There is substantial discussion of what factors determine the scaling
examples.translation: Ada diskusi substantif tentang faktor apa yang menentukan penskalaan
examples.suggested: Kursus ini juga membahas secara cukup mendalam faktor-faktor yang menentukan penskalaan
examples.why: This is a false-friend calque. "substantif" means essential or substantive, not extensive, and "Ada diskusi ... tentang faktor apa" reads like stiff translationese.

examples.source: individuals who have some experience with quantum computing
examples.translation: individu yang sudah memiliki sedikit pengalaman dengan komputasi kuantum
examples.suggested: orang-orang yang sudah memiliki pengalaman dengan komputasi kuantum
examples.why: "sedikit" (a little) makes the prerequisite sound smaller than "some" does. "individu" also sounds stiff for course copy.

editor_note: The rewritten heading in entry 13 renders "Support vector machines" as the literal calque "Mesin vektor pendukung". Every body mention on the page keeps the English term: "support vector machine" in entry 4, "support vector machines" in entry 14, and "algoritma support vector machine" in entry 25, and "support vectors" in entry 16 is also left in English. The meaning is correct and a learner would still recognize the concept, so this is not misleading. It is a heading-versus-body inconsistency, and Indonesian ML writing normally uses the English "Support Vector Machine (SVM)", so the heading should match the body.

examples.source: Support vector machines {#support-vector-machines}
examples.translation: Mesin vektor pendukung {#support-vector-machines}
examples.suggested: Support vector machine (SVM) {#support-vector-machines}
examples.why: The heading uses a literal calque, but the body right below it (entry 14) and entries 4 and 25 keep 'support vector machine' in English. Indonesian ML writing conventionally uses the English term, so the heading should match the body.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries match the English and use the informal kamu register, from "mengikuti ujian lencana" (badging exam) in [7] to the privacy notice in [11], which keeps every clause, including "pemroses data pihak ketiga yang diotorisasi oleh IBM", "secara global" and "sesuai dengan praktik privasi IBM".

None of the six rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entries 35, 36 and 54 are faithful, and entry 54 keeps its caveat against running the larger circuit on a fake device. In entry 68, "quantum lead time" becomes "waktu keunggulan kuantum", and next to "pada suatu titik" the sentence parses as "at some point in time, that quantum advantage becomes important", which loses the idea of a lead time. The same entry also switches between "quantum advantage" and "keunggulan kuantum". Entry 65 uses inclusive "Kita menyediakan" where the authors mean exclusive "Kami", and entry 56's "Kamu melihat" is a stiff calque of "You see".

examples.line_approx: hingga pada suatu titik waktu keunggulan kuantum itu menjadi sangat penting
examples.source: until at some point that quantum lead time becomes critically important
examples.translation: hingga pada suatu titik waktu keunggulan kuantum itu menjadi sangat penting
examples.suggested: hingga pada suatu saat selisih waktu keunggulan kuantum tersebut menjadi sangat penting
examples.why: 'titik waktu' merges with 'pada suatu', so the sentence reads as 'quantum advantage becomes important' and loses the lead-time idea. The entry also uses both 'quantum advantage' and 'keunggulan kuantum'.

examples.source: We provide the values for the "mitigated" points
examples.translation: Kita menyediakan nilai-nilai untuk titik-titik "yang dimitigasi"
examples.suggested: Kami menyediakan nilai-nilai titik "yang dimitigasi"
examples.why: The authors, not the reader, supply the data, so exclusive 'Kami' is correct. Entry 54 already uses 'Kami menyarankan'.

examples.line_approx: Kamu melihat efek bising yang parah
examples.source: You see the severe effects of noise on FakeToronto.
examples.translation: Kamu melihat efek bising yang parah pada FakeToronto.
examples.suggested: Terlihat jelas dampak bising yang parah pada FakeToronto.
examples.why: 'Kamu melihat' is a literal calque of the English 'You see'. An Indonesian technical writer would use 'Terlihat' or 'Kamu dapat melihat'.

editor_note: All five rewritten entries match their English and use the informal "kamu" register. Entry 21 keeps the 6-qubit setup, the "memang mendominasi, tapi errornya cukup besar" caveat and the "lebih dari 50%" threshold; the 16- and 30-qubit counts in entries 44 and 57 are correct; entry 85 keeps "tiga ide".

The five rewritten entries (41, 44, 46, 58, 61) keep their meaning. The survival-probability definition, the complement plot (1 - P) and its lower-bar-is-better reading, and the caveat that mirror circuits do not scale are all correct, so a learner would not be misled. A native editor would still fix some wording in entry 61. "sinyal yang tersisa kecil didominasi" has the adjective in the wrong place and reads awkwardly; it should be "sinyal kecil yang tersisa didominasi". "menghancurkan" ("destroys") is stronger than "overwhelms", so "menenggelamkan" fits better. In entry 41, "sedikit berpengaruh" is ambiguous. Changing it to "hanya sedikit berpengaruh" makes the "little effect" meaning clear.

examples.source: the small surviving signal is dominated by accumulated error
examples.translation: sinyal yang tersisa kecil didominasi oleh accumulated error
examples.suggested: sinyal kecil yang tersisa didominasi oleh error yang terakumulasi
examples.why: The adjective is in the wrong place, so the sentence reads as 'the remaining signal [is] small, dominated...'. It should say 'the small remaining signal'.

examples.source: the depolarizing noise accumulated across the mirror circuit overwhelms most of the signal
examples.translation: noise depolarizing yang terakumulasi di seluruh mirror circuit menghancurkan sebagian besar sinyal
examples.suggested: noise depolarizing yang terakumulasi di seluruh mirror circuit menenggelamkan sebagian besar sinyal
examples.why: 'menghancurkan' (destroys) goes further than 'overwhelms'. 'menenggelamkan' (drowns out) matches the signal-versus-noise meaning.

examples.source: so circuit size has little effect on its transpilation time at this scale
examples.translation: sehingga ukuran Circuit sedikit berpengaruh pada waktu transpilasi di skala ini
examples.suggested: sehingga ukuran Circuit hanya sedikit berpengaruh pada waktu transpilasinya di skala ini
examples.why: Without 'hanya', 'sedikit berpengaruh' can read as 'has some effect' instead of 'has little effect'. Adding 'hanya' keeps the intended stress on how small the effect is.

editor_note: None of the six rewritten entries (24, 39, 44, 47, 48, 50) would mislead a learner. They keep the phase -1 definition, the X-gates-as-open-control equivalence, the exponential growth of two-qubit depth, the O(sqrt(2^n)) iteration count and the fault-tolerant framing. Two phrasings would still be changed by a native editor. In entry 47, "tumbuh sebesar $O(\sqrt{2^n})$" reads as "grows by an amount of", so "tumbuh sebanding dengan" or "berskala $O(...)" is better. In entry 44, "Untuk alasan ini" is a calque of "For this reason", and "Karena itu" is the natural form.

examples.source: the optimal number of Grover iterations itself grows as $O(\sqrt{2^n})$
examples.translation: jumlah iterasi Grover yang optimal sendiri tumbuh sebesar $O(\sqrt{2^n})$
examples.suggested: jumlah iterasi Grover yang optimal itu sendiri tumbuh sebanding dengan $O(\sqrt{2^n})$
examples.why: 'tumbuh sebesar' suggests growth by a fixed amount rather than asymptotic scaling. 'sebanding dengan' states the Big-O growth relation clearly.

examples.source: For this reason, we demonstrate the hardware execution at the same small scale
examples.translation: Untuk alasan ini, kita mendemonstrasikan eksekusi hardware pada skala kecil yang sama
examples.suggested: Karena itu, kita mendemonstrasikan eksekusi di hardware pada skala kecil yang sama
examples.why: 'Untuk alasan ini' is a literal calque of the English. Indonesian technical prose normally uses 'Karena itu' or 'Oleh karena itu'.

editor_note: All five rewritten entries (62, 66, 144, 149, 223) match the English: r=10 with 5 Trotter steps, the Toeplitz first-row reconstruction, depth 15→6 and infidelity 0.045 vs 0.075 at reps=8 are all correct, and terms stay consistent with the rest of the page (keadaan dasar, circuit terdalam, gate evolusi waktu terkontrol → versi bebas-kontrol).

None of the 7 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The weak-coupling argument in [25], the LSH quantum numbers and parity-dependent n_f definition in [22], and the usage caveat in [4] all keep their meaning. Entry [8] uses the English "primitive" where the rest of the page says "primitif" ([11], [60], [88]). In [25], "favors states with large n_l" became "menguntungkan state", a literal choice that sounds odd in physics prose, and "hopping tetangga terdekat murni lokal" stacks the modifiers in an order that reads stiffly. [22] turns "A key challenge" into "Tantangan utamanya" ("the main challenge"), which slightly overstates the English.

examples.source: using the Qiskit Estimator primitive
examples.translation: menggunakan primitive Qiskit Estimator
examples.suggested: menggunakan primitif Qiskit Estimator
examples.why: The rest of the file uses 'primitif' ([11], [60], [88]), so this rewritten entry breaks consistency.

examples.source: which favors states with large $n_l$ ... reduces to a purely local nearest-neighbor hopping
examples.translation: yang menguntungkan state dengan $n_l$ besar ... tereduksi menjadi hopping tetangga terdekat murni lokal
examples.suggested: yang cenderung memilih state dengan $n_l$ besar ... tereduksi menjadi hopping antar-tetangga terdekat yang murni lokal
examples.why: 'Menguntungkan' (benefits) is a literal rendering of 'favors' that is odd in physics prose, and the modifier stack is stiff.

examples.source: A key challenge is that
examples.translation: Tantangan utamanya adalah
examples.suggested: Salah satu tantangan utama adalah
examples.why: The English says 'a key challenge', not 'the main challenge'. The difference is small but it overstates the claim.

editor_note: All five rewritten entries (4, 9, 57, 60, 64) keep their meaning. Entry 57 still says the benefit shows up only on noisy hardware ("Manfaat backpropagation baru terlihat pada hardware yang berderau"), entry 60 keeps the caveat about error vs. noise reduction ("agar kesalahan aproksimasi tidak mengalahkan pengurangan derau"), and truncation→pemangkasan matches the rest of the page.

None of the 25 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The key claims all match the English: transpiling before cutting avoids transpiling every subexperiment, the virtual coupling map avoids extra SWAP gates, the sampling overhead of 6 gives 6^num_reps subexperiments, and the caveat that no error suppression or mitigation was used is kept. What remains is small polish. 'Z-type' is left in English next to Indonesian 'berbobot-1/berbobot-2' in entries 49, 52 and 57, which reads as a half-translated calque. Entry 51 uses 'instance' where entry 8 uses 'instans'. Entry 51 also opens with the stiff subjectless 'Berguna untuk memverifikasi silang ... dibandingkan tanpa pemotongan'.

examples.source: the average of weight-1 and weight-2 Z-type observables
examples.translation: rata-rata dari observable Z-type berbobot-1 dan berbobot-2
examples.suggested: rata-rata observable tipe-Z berbobot-1 dan berbobot-2
examples.why: English 'Z-type' is kept next to Indonesian 'berbobot', which gives a mixed calque. 'tipe-Z' reads naturally. The same fix applies in entries 52 and 57.

examples.source: This allows a homogenous usage of primitive over all the instances.
examples.translation: Hal ini memungkinkan penggunaan primitif yang seragam di semua instance.
examples.suggested: Hal ini memungkinkan penggunaan primitif yang seragam di semua instans.
examples.why: Entry 8 uses the Indonesian spelling 'instans' but this entry keeps the English 'instance', so the file is inconsistent.

examples.source: It is useful to cross-verify the advantage of the circuit cutting technique against uncut.
examples.translation: Berguna untuk memverifikasi silang keunggulan teknik circuit cutting dibandingkan tanpa pemotongan.
examples.suggested: Ada gunanya memverifikasi silang keunggulan teknik circuit cutting dibandingkan dengan Circuit yang tidak dipotong.
examples.why: The sentence has no subject and ends with the clipped comparison 'dibandingkan tanpa pemotongan', which copies the English shorthand 'against uncut'. A native technical writer would name the thing being compared.

editor_note: None of the five rewritten entries (20, 21, 57, 66, 74) would mislead a learner. They keep the meaning, the caveats and the gate_folding/pea distinction. The one thing a native editor would fix is in entry 74: "dua-qubit basis gate" appears twice and keeps the English modifier-first order. Indonesian puts the head noun first ("basis gate dua-qubit"), and the rest of the page already does this ("Gate dua-Qubit" in entries 33 and 49). Entry 66 also has a small inconsistency: it says "tata letak qubit" in one sentence and "layout ini" two sentences later for the same concept.

examples.source: which amplifies by repeating two-qubit basis gates ... for layers of twirled two-qubit basis gates
examples.translation: yang memperkuat dengan mengulang dua-qubit basis gate ... untuk lapisan dua-qubit basis gate yang di-twirl
examples.suggested: yang memperkuat dengan mengulang basis gate dua-qubit ... untuk lapisan basis gate dua-qubit yang di-twirl
examples.why: This copies the English modifier-first word order. Indonesian puts the head noun first, and the rest of the page already writes "Gate dua-Qubit".

examples.source: The information about the qubit layout is stored ... you need to apply this layout to the observable
examples.translation: Informasi tentang tata letak qubit disimpan ... kamu perlu menerapkan layout ini ke observabel
examples.suggested: ... kamu perlu menerapkan tata letak ini ke observabel
examples.why: The same concept is called "tata letak" and then "layout" within one paragraph. Using one term reads more cleanly.

editor_note: The three rewritten entries (15, 38, 63) are faithful and read naturally: "mitigasi kesalahan kuasi-probabilistik yang efisien dan tidak bias", "lalu kita potong lapisannya sesuai jumlah qubit" and "mitigasi kesalahan bebas bias pada perangkat kuantum yang noisy" all keep the English meaning, and none drops a caveat.

Entry 10 keeps the English meaning: nothing is inverted, softened or made up. It does have three problems a native editor would fix. First, it leaves ordinary English nouns in the running text ("tools", "insight", "lithium–sulfur"), even though entry 9 already uses "litium", and plain Indonesian words exist for all of them ("alat", "wawasan", "litium–sulfur"). Second, it uses "permukaan energi potensial" while the rest of the page keeps "potential energy surface (PES)". Third, the closing phrase "proses kimia yang lebih efisien sumber daya" is a stiff calque; "lebih hemat sumber daya" reads more naturally.

examples.source: More broadly, potential energy surfaces are tools for studying reaction pathways and catalysts for more resource-efficient chemical processes.
examples.translation: Secara lebih luas, permukaan energi potensial adalah tools untuk mempelajari jalur reaksi dan katalis untuk proses kimia yang lebih efisien sumber daya.
examples.suggested: Secara lebih luas, potential energy surface (PES) merupakan alat untuk mempelajari jalur reaksi dan katalis bagi proses kimia yang lebih hemat sumber daya.
examples.why: The lowercase English 'tools' is left in the middle of an Indonesian sentence for no reason. 'efisien sumber daya' is a calque. The PES term also differs from the one used everywhere else on the page.

examples.source: Calculating how energy changes as a Li–S bond breaks provides molecular-level insight relevant to understanding the chemical transformations in these systems.
examples.translation: Menghitung bagaimana energi berubah saat ikatan Li–S putus memberikan insight tingkat molekuler yang relevan untuk memahami transformasi kimia dalam sistem ini.
examples.suggested: Menghitung perubahan energi saat ikatan Li–S putus memberikan wawasan tingkat molekuler yang relevan untuk memahami transformasi kimia dalam sistem-sistem ini.
examples.why: 'insight' has a standard Indonesian equivalent, 'wawasan'. 'Menghitung bagaimana energi berubah' follows English word order too closely.

examples.source: The lithium–sulfur example connects this workflow to research on next-generation batteries for energy storage.
examples.translation: Contoh lithium–sulfur menghubungkan workflow ini dengan penelitian tentang baterai generasi berikutnya untuk penyimpanan energi.
examples.suggested: Contoh litium–sulfur menghubungkan alur kerja ini dengan penelitian tentang baterai generasi berikutnya untuk penyimpanan energi.
examples.why: Entry 9 already spells the element the Indonesian way, 'litium', so the English spelling 'lithium' here is inconsistent.

editor_note: The three rewritten entries (24, 45, 51) keep the English meaning, including the caveat in 51 that updated device information "menjadi semakin berkurang" in importance as chain length grows. Entry 45 renders the garbled "number lengths of RB experiments" sensibly as "jumlah dan panjang sekuens eksperimen RB".

The five rewritten entries (13, 27, 42, 51, 66) keep their meaning. Nothing in them would mislead a learner: the zig-zag mapping, the ancilla at every 4th spatial orbital, the warning when alpha-beta pairs can't be implemented and the heavy-hex/square split by processor family all match the English. Three small wording fixes remain. Entry 13 leaves "sustainability" in English where "keberlanjutan" is the normal Indonesian word. Entry 66 uses "dimensi subspace" while the rest of the page uses "subruang" (entries 15, 33). Entry 27 renders "is present" as the calque "hadir", where "terdapat" would read more naturally.

examples.source: connects this example to sustainability through ammonia production
examples.translation: menghubungkan contoh ini dengan sustainability melalui produksi amonia
examples.suggested: menghubungkan contoh ini dengan isu keberlanjutan melalui produksi amonia
examples.why: 'Sustainability' is an ordinary word, not a technical term. Indonesian readers would expect 'keberlanjutan', so leaving it in English reads as untranslated.

examples.source: to allow larger subspace dimensions
examples.translation: untuk memungkinkan dimensi subspace yang lebih besar
examples.suggested: untuk memungkinkan dimensi subruang yang lebih besar
examples.why: The rest of the page renders 'subspace' as 'subruang' (entries 15, 33), so this is an inconsistency within the file.

examples.source: a connection between orbitals of different spin is present at every 4th spatial orbital
examples.translation: koneksi antara orbital dengan spin berbeda hadir pada setiap orbital spasial ke-4
examples.suggested: terdapat koneksi antara orbital dengan spin berbeda pada setiap orbital spasial ke-4
examples.why: 'hadir' is a literal copy of 'is present'. Indonesian technical writing would use 'terdapat' or 'ada'.

editor_note: None of the 8 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The phase-estimation walkthrough (22), the failure causes k=0 and non-coprime k, r (59), the even-r condition (66) and the resource estimates (74) all keep their meaning. Entry 66 leaves "greatest common divisor" in English, where the standard Indonesian term is "faktor persekutuan terbesar (FPB)". The same entry copies "otherwise" as "jika tidak" right after a "Jika r tidak genap" clause, so it reads more naturally if it states the condition outright. Entry 61 has the calque "Di sini kita beralih ke" and the clipped "secara linear bukan kuadratik". Entry 76 keeps the English "Fig. 9" / "Fig. 2" instead of "Gambar 9" / "Gambar 2".

examples.source: otherwise, there is a high probability that the greatest common divisor of $N$ and either $a^{r/2}-1$, or $a^{r/2}+1$ is a proper factor of $N$.
examples.translation: jika tidak, ada probabilitas tinggi bahwa greatest common divisor dari $N$ dan salah satu dari $a^{r/2}-1$, atau $a^{r/2}+1$ adalah faktor sejati dari $N$.
examples.suggested: jika $r$ genap, besar kemungkinan faktor persekutuan terbesar (FPB) dari $N$ dengan $a^{r/2}-1$ atau $a^{r/2}+1$ merupakan faktor sejati dari $N$.
examples.why: Indonesian math has a standard term for gcd (FPB) that learners know from school. Also, 'jika tidak' placed right after 'Jika r tidak genap' leaves it unclear which case it refers to, so it is clearer to name the condition.

examples.source: Here we turn to dynamical decoupling (DD) for error suppression ... which accumulate linearly rather than quadratically.
examples.translation: Di sini kita beralih ke [dynamical decoupling] (DD) untuk penekanan error ... yang terakumulasi secara linear bukan kuadratik.
examples.suggested: Di sini kita menggunakan [dynamical decoupling] (DD) untuk penekanan error ... yang terakumulasi secara linear, bukan kuadratik.
examples.why: 'beralih ke' is a literal copy of 'turn to' and suggests switching away from something. The contrast clause also needs a comma, or 'alih-alih', to read naturally.

examples.source: read about the methodologies shown in Fig. 9 of [6] and Fig. 2 of [7].
examples.translation: membaca tentang metodologi yang ditunjukkan di Fig. 9 dari [[6]] dan Fig. 2 dari [[7]].
examples.suggested: membaca metodologi yang ditunjukkan pada Gambar 9 di [[6]] dan Gambar 2 di [[7]].
examples.why: The English abbreviation 'Fig.' was left in running Indonesian prose. The Indonesian label is 'Gambar'.

editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries (7, 26, 32, 34) would mislead a learner. Entries 7, 32 and 34 are faithful and natural: the "lower costs mean better" logic and "jauh mengungguli pemilihan acak" match the English. Entry 26 has two problems. It writes "algoritma quantum hybrid" and "sirkuit quantum" with the English spelling, while the rest of the page, including the rewritten entry 32, uses "kuantum". It also renders "error suppression" as "suppression error", which keeps English word order inside an Indonesian phrase; a native editor would write "supresi error" or "penekanan error".

examples.source: mapping the problem to a hybrid quantum algorithm, running the quantum circuits
examples.translation: pemetaan masalah ke algoritma quantum hybrid, menjalankan sirkuit quantum
examples.suggested: pemetaan masalah ke algoritma kuantum hibrida, menjalankan sirkuit kuantum
examples.why: This entry spells it 'quantum', but the rest of the page, including entries 0, 8 and 32, uses 'kuantum'.

examples.source: running the quantum circuits with error suppression
examples.translation: menjalankan sirkuit quantum dengan suppression error
examples.suggested: menjalankan sirkuit kuantum dengan supresi error
examples.why: 'suppression error' copies the English words and word order. Indonesian puts the head noun first, so 'supresi error' or 'penekanan error'.
